money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Armenian Dram (AMD). Strict rules apply to importing and exporting cash amounts of USD 10,000 or over (or equivalent). US dollars and euros can be exchanged at banks. ATMs and credit card facilities are available in Yerevan but are less common outside major towns.

laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are severe. They include long prison sentences.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Always carry a copy of your passport. Police can stop you to check your documents. It's illegal to take photos of: government or military sites monuments officers in uniform
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: To drive, you need both: a valid International Driving Permit (IDP) a valid Australian driver's licence (digital driver’s licences may not be accepted) Get your IDP before you leave Australia. Driving without an IDP could void your travel and vehicle insurance.
laws.heading: Driving permit

laws.rule: Cash or travellers' cheques up to USD 10,000 (about A$14,200 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = USD 0.7040) need no declaration on entering Armenia. Monetary instruments other than travellers' cheques must be declared whatever the amount. Funds on bank cards are not declared. Above USD 100,000, documents showing where the funds came from are required. The guide gives no penalty.
laws.heading: Cash declaration

laws.rule: The State Revenue Committee's guide says bringing in more than 5 litres of alcohol or drinks over 0.5% alcohol from third countries is prohibited, as is import by anyone under 18. Above 3 litres, a declaration and customs duty of the AMD equivalent of EUR 10 a litre are required.
laws.heading: Alcohol limits on entry

laws.rule: The State Revenue Committee's guide says it is prohibited to bring in more than 200 cigarettes, 50 cigars or cigarillos, 200 heated tobacco sticks, or 250 g of tobacco products in total, and prohibited for anyone under 18. It gives no separate rule on e-cigarettes.
laws.heading: Tobacco limits on entry

laws.rule: The State Revenue Committee's guide says medicines for personal treatment may be brought in without certification up to 10 types with three consumer packs each, if the prescription or doctor's document does not justify more. Narcotic or psychotropic medicines need medical documents (with a name and quantity; certified and notarised Armenian translations if in another language) and a customs declaration, and only those registered in Armenia may be brought in.
laws.heading: Medicines on entry

laws.rule: The State Revenue Committee's guide says up to 5 kg of pre-packaged animal products may be brought in without a veterinary certificate, if the factory packaging is intact. Up to 2 dogs or cats need no special permit if the pet passport shows a clinical examination within 14 days before shipment.
laws.heading: Animal products
